chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The caravan of the Imam (peace be upon him) was delayed between Arafat and Muzdalifah, so he stopped and prayed the Maghrib prayer, and prayed the 'Isha prayer in Muzdalifah.

key_terms.عَثَرَ: To be delayed or hindered in travel
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: Arafat, a key station in Hajj
key_terms.مَحْمِلُ أَبِي: The caravan of the Imam (peace be upon him)
key_terms.وَالْمُزْدَلِفَةِ: And Muzdalifah, the second key station in Hajj

ai.seo_question: How did the Imam combine prayers during Hajj when delayed between Arafat and Muzdalifah?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the jurisprudential basis for combining Maghrib and 'Isha prayers during the Hajj journey between Arafat and Muzdalifah, specifically highlighting the practice of praying 'Isha in Muzdalifah rather than Arafat. It underscores the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding travel-related prayer combinations (Jam' al-Safar) and aligns with the broader ritual of the Hajj where pilgrims spend the night at Muzdalifah before proceeding to Mina. The hadith serves as a key evidence for the permissibility of delaying 'Isha to be prayed with Maghrib in this specific context, reflecting the practical realities of the pilgrimage route.
